the semantic structure of the LTM network is a scale-free network and the semantic structure of LTM network can be described as a small-world network.
the information retrieval from L TM shows that the entire network can be considered to act as an information amplifier which, in turn, leads to the emergence (in time) of new cognitive structures.

(1) a dynamical model of information retrieval based upon a long-term memory network is able to reproduce the power-law behavior and the scale-free graph properties observed in the real world; (2) this model can be considered to represent an information amplifier, which leads to the appearance of new cognitive structures.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to knowledge representation and information retrieval, based upon a dynamical model of long-term memory.
the study of the dynamical properties of the user-network system, and the analysis of the emerging structures.
a new model of information retrieval which is a first attempt to understand the dynamics of the information flow in an LTM network and its role in the emergence of new semantic domains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LTM network can be considered as a dynamical system that is able to amplify the amount of information in the environment.
the information retrieval process is a self-organized process which leads the system to a new equilibrium state, characterized by an increase in its complexity.
the information retrieval is not a passive operation, but it can lead to a new knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information retrieval from a LTM network is a dynamical process, where the network structure and the semantic domain are co-evolving.
the information retrieval from a LTM network is a process of information amplification which leads to the emerging of new cognitive structures, in which the entire user-network system is involved.
the information retrieval from LTTM is a process which leads to an amplification of the information content of the system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information retrieval is not a static process and the cognitive structures are dynamic and evolving.

a cognitive system is a dynamical system and that a dynamical model of information retrieval is a key point in order to explain the emergence of new structures and the formation of scale-free clusters.
the dynamical interplay between system and environment is the key to understanding how the information retrieval process works.
